questions.stem: What is the role of starch stores in a germinating seed?

options.text: They provide structural support for the growing shoot
They are converted into glucose by enzymes to provide energy for growth
They absorb water to help the seed swell
They protect the embryo from disease

questions.explanation: Starch stored in the seed is broken down into glucose by the enzyme amylase. The glucose is then used in respiration to release energy for the growth of the embryo before it can photosynthesise.
